title: BioR5: A Three-Layer Architecture for Biological Reasoning in Scientific AI
problem: Biological research requires diverse reasoning modes (phylogenetic analysis, mechanistic understanding, etc.), but current AI systems employ single methodologies, limiting effectiveness in complex biological domains.
motivation: Biology is multifaceted – requires specialized reasoning modes not available in monolithic LLMs. Need architecture supporting multiple reasoning strategies with intelligent mode selection.
method: Three-layer architecture with eleven distinct biological reasoning modes. Layer A: parametric memory (LLMs). Layer B: specialized foundation models for multimodal data. Layer C: external databases and computational tools. Intelligent reasoning mode selection combining keyword matching and LLM analysis.
key_novelty: Multi-mode architecture for biological reasoning; specialized tool integration; automatic reasoning mode selection; biology-specific reasoning mode catalog (11 modes); open-source framework supporting dynamic mode registration.
contributions: BioR5 three-layer architecture for biological AI systems
Eleven biological reasoning modes with intelligent triage
Integration of specialized foundation models + external tools
Toxicology specialization demonstration with TX-Gemma, PubChem, ToxCast, ChEMBL
limitations: Abstract-only evaluation; only toxicology specialization demonstrated; scalability to 11 modes unclear; no quantitative performance metrics provided
